criticFindings.evidence: The script lists applications but does not explain the underlying mechanisms or how ML algorithms achieve these results, which limits the teaching of intuition.

criticFindings.problem: Redundant and vague definition of machine learning
criticFindings.evidence: The definition in #1 is nearly identical to the introduction in #0 and lacks depth or explanation of the core concept.
criticFindings.action: Revise the definition to include the core idea of learning from data, pattern recognition, and generalization.

criticFindings.problem: Repetition of the same example without variation
criticFindings.evidence: The same example of electrical load prediction is repeated three times in #2, which lacks pedagogical value and may confuse students.
criticFindings.action: Replace the repeated example with different real-world applications to illustrate the breadth of ML.

criticFindings.evidence: The explanation in #5 mentions the value of ML but does not provide intuition or examples of how it helps in creating complex systems or understanding human learning.
criticFindings.action: Add intuitive examples and explain how ML contributes to cognitive science with concrete analogies.

criticFindings.problem: Lack of explanation of the learning process
criticFindings.evidence: The definition in #7 is brief and does not explain how the model learns the relationship between inputs and outputs.
criticFindings.action: Add an explanation of the learning process, such as how the model iteratively improves its predictions.

criticFindings.evidence: The definition in #8 mentions clustering but does not explain what it is or how it is performed.
criticFindings.action: Add an intuitive explanation of clustering and its purpose in unsupervised learning.

criticFindings.problem: Lack of explanation of the environment and reward mechanism
criticFindings.evidence: The definition in #9 mentions reinforcement learning but does not explain the environment or how rewards are used to guide learning.
criticFindings.action: Add an explanation of the environment, reward, and how the agent learns through trial and error.

criticFindings.problem: Lack of grounding in source scope
criticFindings.evidence: The generalized framework in #10 is presented without reference to foundational sources or literature, which could mislead students about its theoretical basis.
criticFindings.action: Cite foundational sources or literature that define the three components of the ML framework.

criticFindings.problem: Lack of depth in explanation of the learning process
criticFindings.evidence: The recap in #11 mentions loss functions and optimization but does not explain how they work or their role in the learning process.
criticFindings.action: Add an intuitive explanation of loss functions and optimization techniques, such as gradient descent.

blocks.title: Definition of Machine Learning
blocks.teachingObjective: Machine learning is a field of study that enables computers to learn without being explicitly programmed.

blocks.teachingObjective: Machine learning is applied in real-life scenarios such as smart assistants, advertising, and electrical load prediction.

blocks.title: Why Study Machine Learning

blocks.title: Big Picture of Machine Learning

blocks.title: Supervised Learning

blocks.title: Unsupervised Learning
